job.title: Real-World Evidence Strategy Lead, Dermatology (Belgium) @ UCB (Anderlecht, BRU, BE)
job.description:
**Make your mark for patients**

We are looking for a **Real-World Evidence Strategy Lead, Dermatology** who is **strategic, collaborative and impact-driven** to join us in our **Real-World Evidence team**, based at our headquarters in **Anderlecht, Brussels, Belgium**. This is a **hybrid role requiring 40% weekly onsite presence.**

**About the role**

As a Real-World Evidence Strategy Lead, you will shape and deliver evidence strategies supporting assets within Dermatology. You will translate prioritized research questions into impactful real-world evidence, outcomes research and data strategies supporting clinical, regulatory, access and patient-centered decisions. This strategic role combines scientific expertise with cross-functional leadership, helping ensure evidence is relevant and fit for purpose for different stakeholders throughout the product lifecycle.

**Who you’ll work with**

You will be working in a highly collaborative environment, partnering across global development, safety, payer evidence, regional medical and patient-focused teams. You will also build relationships with external experts, influencers and research partners, while providing leadership and mentorship across the wider Global Real-World Evidence function.

**What you’ll do**

* Develop strategic real-world evidence plans supporting clinical, regulatory, access and patient needs.
* Anticipate evidence gaps and identify innovative solutions across the product lifecycle.
* Lead real-world evidence studies, ensuring quality, governance, timelines and budget delivery.
* Partner across functions to align evidence strategies and stakeholder requirements.
* Build productive relationships with external experts, influencers and research partners.
* Lead and develop experts while supporting broader functional leadership and mentorship.

**Interested? For this role we’re looking for the following education, experience and skills**

* Advanced degree in life sciences, medicine, epidemiology, statistics or related discipline.
* At least eight years of relevant pharmaceutical industry experience, preferably having worked in Dermatology and Immunology space
* Strong expertise in epidemiology, outcomes research and real-world evidence methodologies.
* Experience developing evidence strategies across clinical development, regulatory and market access.
* Strong cross-functional leadership, influencing, communication and stakeholder management skills and having lead teams
* Been a strong contributor or has lead Integrated Evidence roles
* Excellent written and spoken English, with proven scientific communication capabilities.

Are you ready to ‘go beyond’ to create value and make your mark for patients? If this sounds like you, then we would love to hear from you!

**About us**  
UCB is a global biopharmaceutical company, focusing on neurology and immunology. We are over 9.000 people in all four corners of the globe, inspired by patients and driven by science.

**Why work with us?**  
At UCB, we don’t just complete tasks, we create value. We aren’t afraid to push forward, collaborate, and innovate to make our mark for patients. We have a caring, supportive culture where everyone feels included, respected, and has equal opportunities to do their best work. We ‘go beyond’ to create value for our patients, and always with a human focus, whether that’s on our patients, our employees, or our planet. Working for us, you will discover a place where you can grow, and have the freedom to carve your own career path to achieve your full potential.

At UCB, we’ve embraced a hybrid-first approach to work, bringing teams together in local hubs to foster collaborative curiosity. Unless expressly stated in the description or precluded by the nature of the position, roles are hybrid with 40% of your time spent in the office.

job.title: Rethink Plastic Alliance Communications Coordinator (Cover) for the Break Free From Plastic movement @ Zero Waste Europe (Brussels, BRU, BE)
job.description:
**WE'RE RECRUITING!**

**Rethink Plastic Alliance Communications Coordinator (Cover)for the Break Free From Plastic movement in Europe**

**About the Break Free From Plastic movement**

Break Free From Plastic (BFFP) is a global movement envisioning a future free from plastic pollution. Since its launch in September 2016, over 3500 organisations from 186 countries have joined the movement to demand massive reductions in single-use plastics and to push for lasting solutions to the plastic pollution crisis. In Europe, the movement counts 132 members in 33 countries, coordinating their work to achieve systemic change. Zero Waste Europe (ZWE) hosts the coordination team of the European chapter of the movement.

**About the Rethink Plastic Alliance**

The Rethink Plastic Alliance (RPA) acts as the policy arm of the European BFFP movement. RPA is made up of nine BFFP members who work together to advocate for effective EU policies to tackle plastic pollution along the whole lifecycle of plastics. This includes EU policies related to plastic production and (petro-)chemicals, microplastics, health impacts of plastic pollution, and broader policies related to the circular economy, including waste prevention and reuse and recycling. Members of the Alliance are: Center for International Environmental Law (CIEL), ClientEarth, the Environmental Investigation Agency (EIA), the European Environment Bureau (EEB), the European Environmental Citizen’s Organisation for Standardisation (ECOS), Greenpeace, Seas At Risk, Surfrider Foundation Europe, and Zero Waste Europe.

**You**

You are passionate about tackling plastic pollution and its root causes, and you know how to turn complex EU policy issues into communication outputs that decision-makers understand and act on. You are an experienced communicator and skilled writer who is equally comfortable writing a press release, running a social media campaign, managing a website and coordinating a newsletter. You enjoy working in coalitions: bringing diverse partners together, finding the shared message and helping a network speak with one voice. You are organised, proactive and good at juggling several workstreams, and you can spot an opportunity in the news cycle and turn it into a timely, creative response. You work well with colleagues across Europe and the globe, and you like being part of an agile, collaborative team.

**The Role**

This is a temporary position, covering the role for up to 15 months. The post is being created because the current postholder has been temporarily promoted into a cover role within the team, and we need cover for her position. We anticipate the role lasting at least one year, but we can currently only offer an initial fixed-term contract of 6 months, followed by extensions of 3 months at a time. The Rethink Plastic Alliance (RPA) Communications Coordinator (Cover) leads the development, implementation and evaluation of communications for the Rethink Plastic Alliance, working closely with Alliance members and the RPA Policy Coordinator. The role covers the full range of communications work, from managing the Alliance’s website, social media and newsletter to coordinating press releases, publications and events.

The Communications Coordinator also ensures that RPA communications are aligned with the wider BFFP European and global movement. The role includes overseeing third-party contractors and contributing to the wider BFFP Europe coordination team.

**Key Responsibilities**

Coordinate communications of the Rethink Plastic Alliance (40%)

* Develop, implement and evaluate effective communication plans and campaigns for RPA, in close coordination with RPA members and the RPA Policy Coordinator
* Coordinate the production of the RPA’s communications materials, including publications and press releases. This includes providing support to RPA members in the form of drafting and disseminating publications and press releases, as relevant. It also involves corresponding with key journalists and handling press requests by connecting journalists and RPA experts.
* Coordinate the promotion of and communications around RPA online and in-person events.
* Plan and facilitate the RPA Communications Group meetings (approx. 6 per year), and liaise with RPA Communications Group and facilitate follow up from meetings
* Support the RPA Policy Coordinator with the planning of regular policy-focused meetings by providing input, contributing to planning, agenda-setting and follow up
* Support the RPA Policy Coordinator with the planning, agenda setting and preparation of the whole-day RPA Strategy Days (held twice a year) and facilitate communications-related sessions.
* Produce RPA’s quarterly newsletter, presenting the advocacy work of RPA in an accessible manner and featuring RPA member updates.
* Develop suitable messaging for RPA campaigns in response to external events and developments, by adapting the RPA Messaging Guide.
* Support the RPA Policy Coordinator with the final drafting of the RPA Strategy, taking into account member inputs gathered in an ongoing process.

Manage Rethink Plastic Alliance communications tools (25%)

* Run RPA’s daily communications, in line with its advocacy strategy.
* Manage RPA’s website, which includes technical website management, sharing RPA publications and press releases on the website, producing content for the website, as well as ensuring the website is running smoothly, by fixing bugs and being in touch with website developers when necessary.
* Manage RPA’s social media channels and online community, by producing and sharing digital multimedia content for Social Media and blog posts for RPA’s website This includes amplifying content by RPA and BFFP members.
* Manage the RPA shared calendar by adding joint RPA and individual member’s campaigns and tracking policy developments (with support from BFFP & RPA Policy Coordinator).
* Ensure smooth communication and access to RPA tools through day-to-day coordination on Slack, especially with members of the RPA Comms group, and by managing the RPA Comms Google Drive.

Ensure coordination with BFFP communications (20%)

* Identify and leverage synergies between the EU policy focused communications from RPA and the work and communications of the wider BFFP movement in Europe (and beyond), together with the BFFP Europe Communications Officer.
* Coordinate with BFFP Europe Communications Officer on any joint RPA-BFFP publications.
* Produce Social Media toolkits for BFFP members at key EU advocacy moments.
* Oversee the work of third-party contractors for some projects, where relevant (i.e. graphic designers, web administrators, contractors, etc.).
* Manage the RPA’s annual communications budget as well as any campaign-specific communications budget.

Contribute to the BFFP Europe coordination team, and the wider team (15%)

* Participate in weekly BFFP Europe Coordination Team meetings and support monthly online BFFP member meetings.
* Provide input for and contribute to the planning, agenda-setting and follow-up of BFFP events.
* Contribute to the drafting of funding proposals and reporting, specifically of comms-related activities.
* Participate in and contribute to global BFFP team quarterly meetings.
* Provide input for and participate in global team retreats, members’ meetings and team planning meetings, where appropriate.
* Contribute to implementing BFFP’s upcoming Global Strategy, where appropriate.

**Person Specification**

Experience

*Essential*

* Substantial experience in communications, ideally for a campaign, advocacy, coalition or non-profit organisation.
* Experience developing and implementing communications strategies and campaigns.
* Experience writing and producing press releases, newsletters and web and social media content.
* Experience managing a website (e.g. a CMS) and social media channels.
* Experience working with journalists and handling media requests.
* Experience working with, or coordinating, groups, networks or coalitions.
* Experience managing freelancers or external contractors (e.g. designers, web developers).

*Desirable*

* Experience in advocacy communications, particularly on EU policy.
* Strong understanding of environmental and climate change topics, including the issues associated with plastic along its supply chain.
* Experience managing small budgets.
* Experience contributing to funding proposals and reports.
* Experience with digital multimedia content production (graphics, short video).
* Experience working with people from different cultures and nationalities.

**Knowledge, skills and understanding**

*Essential*

* Excellent command of English, with the ability to explain complex policy messages clearly to different audiences.
* Excellent writing and editing skills.
* Strategic thinking, with the ability to spot opportunities and synergies and to respond quickly to external events.
* Ability to facilitate meetings and coordinate with many partners at once.
* Strong networking and team-building skills suited to a multicultural, multidisciplinary environment.
* ● Ability to manage competing priorities and meet deadlines.

*Desirable*

* Knowledge of the BFFP movement and/or the Rethink Plastic Alliance.
* Passion for social and environmental justice.
* Understanding of the EU policy-making process and the Brussels environment.
* Excellent organisational skills and attention to detail.
* Solid IT skills with collaborative and communications tools (e.g. Google Drive,
* Slack, Asana, Zoom, Google Groups, newsletter and CMS platforms, Canva or similar).
* Other European languages, apart from English, are a plus.

**Personal qualities**

*Essential*

* Creative, proactive and solution-oriented.
* Excellent interpersonal skills and a team player.
* Excellent listener and communicator.
* Impact-driven and resilient under pressure.
* Organised and able to prioritise.
* Capacity to run several tasks simultaneously.
* Appetite for working in an agile European and international environment.
* Willingness to occasionally work flexible hours and to travel, as required.

**Terms & Conditions, Salary & Benefits**

This is a full-time temporary position (38 hours per week) for up to 15 months based in Belgium (hosted by our fiscal sponsor, Zero Waste Europe. A valid working permit to work in Belgium is required. We offer a gross starting salary of €3.772 per month. In addition to this, we offer the following benefits:

* Lunch vouchers (10€ per day worked: 8,91€ employer contribution, 1,09€ employee contribution)
* 13th month (year end bonus, if applicable)
* Double holiday pay (Belgian standard)
* Hospitalisation, ambulatory and dental insurance (DKV)
* Travel insurance
* Home working and other allowances (170€ net per month)
* Reimbursement of public transport costs for local commuting (max 56 € net per month) upon the production of receipts, full reimbursement of train commuting costs within Belgium, and a bike allowance for commuting by bicycle

BFFP Europe team members also benefit from 26 vacation days plus additional leave between Christmas and New Year, progressive discretionary leave allowances and a 4 day working week (whereby team members are expected to work 90% of their hours for 100% of their pay, and encouraged to do so between Monday and Thursday).

job.title: Project Development Officer (0,8 fte) @ Eindhoven University of Technology (Eindhoven, NB, NL)
job.description:
The Department of Applied Physics and Science Education is a research-driven department housing high-quality educational programs, all featuring strong connections between research and education. Our research is clustered in three focal areas: Fluids, Bio and Soft Matter (FBSM); Plasmas and Beams (PB); and Nano, Quantum and Photonics (NQP). Our shared ambition is to equip the next generation of ‘engineers of the future’ with the knowledge and the skills they will need to impact science, innovation, and society, from regional to global scales.

### **Introduction**

Do you have affinity with physics, scientific research and technology? Are you interested in the semiconductor and related industries? And in energy technologies such as solar cells and batteries? Do you enjoy working with passionate professionals? Are you interested in guiding researchers through the increasingly complex funding landscape? Do you like to build multidisciplinary consortia between researchers and high-tech industry? Do you like to think strategically and empower researchers to realize their research visions? If so, we would like to meet you and explore a possible fit.

### **Job Description**

The Project Development Officer is occupied with all kinds of activities related to proposal development and project management, from acquisition through to the post-award phase. As a project development officer, you support researchers in developing their research ideas into competitive project proposals, reviewing the details of funding calls to determine requirements and eligibility, and coordinating (inter-)national consortia. Once projects are awarded, you play an active role in the post-award phase — arranging legal and contractual documentation, organizing project meetings, and managing project reporting. You will be embedded in the Plasma & Materials Processing research group, which works on nanofabrication technologies for applications in Future Chips and Future Energy. In this role, you work closely with Financial, Legal, and HR colleagues, as well as with project officers and researchers from other departments as part of TU/e's Centers, Institutes, Strategic Areas, and the Research Support Network.

You will be spending part of your time supporting an interdepartmental center and working within the existent Project Office within the Applied Physics and Science Education department. Resulting in a lot of room, freedom and opportunities to fill in and shape your role. And also with space for personal development and growth. Your daily activities consist of:

* Proactively supporting researchers in the acquisition of research projects, including reviewing the details of relevant funding calls to clarify requirements and eligibility;
* Matching opportunities to the expertise and research interests of researchers in the department by communicating current and future developments in both the national and European funding landscape;
* Helping build consortia, by enriching researchers' networks with internal or external collaborators to complete the value chain;
* Supporting proposal writing and applying persuasive writing to maximize proposal chances, while keeping an eye on overall proposal quality;
* Supporting the administrative side of project development and management, including navigating grant rules and setting up budgets (together with TU/e's finance advisors);
* Once projects are awarded, taking an active role in the post-award phase: supporting contract negotiations (together with TU/e's legal counsel), arranging legal and project-related documentation, organizing project meetings, and handling project reporting.

**The Plasma & Materials Processing research group**

The position will be embedded in the Plasma & Materials Processing group, one of the largest research groups in the Department of Applied Physics and Science Education. The group comprises approximately 25 PhD candidates and 10 postdoctoral researchers and is led by six full-time principal investigators. Its expertise centers on nanofabrication technologies, particularly plasma-based processes. The group is internationally recognized for its work on atomic-scale processing methods such as atomic layer deposition and etching. Research is driven by applications in Future Chips (semiconductors, photonics, and quantum technologies) and Future Energy (photovoltaics, batteries, and green hydrogen), supported by strong collaborations with industry.

### **Job Requirements**

* An education in physics, chemistry, nanotechnology, or a related engineering field (at least MSc, but preferably PhD level), with prior research experience — ideally with a proven background or strong affinity for nanotechnology, given the group's research focus.
* Experienced or interested in grant writing;
* Excellent communication skills in English (both oral and written), with the ability to genuinely listen to and understand the needs of every partner involved — researchers, collaborators, and support staff alike;
* A goal-oriented, proactive and hands-on attitude, not afraid of working under deadline pressure;
* An eye for detail;
* Interested in leading and coordinating teams or consortia applying for funding opportunities;
* Curiosity about developments in physics, technology and the funding landscape.

If you are concerned that you don’t meet all the requirements sufficiently, but the job does excite you, then be sure to respond, we would love to look at your profile.

### **Conditions of Employment**

An exciting position within an international yet personal university. You are right in the middle of the students, on a green campus within walking distance of the central station. Besides beautiful architecture, you will find varied workplaces and excellent sports facilities.
  
  
We also offer you:

* In addition to your base salary, you will receive an 8% holiday allowance and an 8.3% year-end bonus, both calculated based on your annual gross base salary.

We are a leading international university where scientific curiosity meets a hands-on mindset.
